newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ mulling rate rise timing - Deputy Gov quoted. [CORRECTED 9:29 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BOJ mulling rate rise timing - Deputy Gov quoted. [CORRECTED 9:29 GMT]

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) Deputy Governor Toshihiko Fukui was quoted by an executive of a labour group as saying on Wednesday that the central bank is considering the right timing to raise the official discount rate but it does not want to make a hasty decision.

Fukui made the remark at a meeting with executives of Japan's largest grouping of labour unions, the Japanese Trade Union Confederation (Rengo), at which the labour group urged the BOJ to raise the discount rate, now at a record low 0.5 percent.
The executive who attended the meeting told reporters that Fukui said the BOJ is now carefully monitoring overall developments in the Japanese economy.

The labour group argued that while Japan's "super-low interest rate policy" had contributed to economic recovery, it had also had adverse effects such as a drop in interest income on people's savings.

Fukui was quoted as saying that the request was understandable. He was also quoted as saying that the April 1 rise in Japan's consumption tax to five percent from three percent may have a gradual impact on consumption.
The peak of disposal of problem loans held at Japanese financial institutions is now over, Fukui was quoted as saying.
Fukui said the economic activities of small and medium-sized companies are not yet robust enough.
Rengo represents eight million workers belonging to labour unions in major industries.

The group said that to continue the current low interest rate policy would be harmful for the Japanese economy, and rates should be raised as early as possible to what it called a proper level. It did not specify what level it wanted to see.
